This nut is found chiefly in hot and humid climates, especially in sea coasts and saltwater shores, and is best known in south-eastern Endor. Even in suitable terrain, it remains hard to find.

The Belan nut is swallowed to stop bleeding, usually within 1–10 rounds. Once bleeding has ceased, the patient must avoid exertion for about an hour. The prepared remedy keeps for three months. Repeated consumption can cause habituation, a separate concern from its immediate ability to stop blood loss.
